I run the agenda and try to keep us to the hour. The director has the final say on money and on the sites. For other decisions, like the form wording, I'm not sure who has the final say, and I'm not sure we know when something has been decided. I can't always tell when a conversation has ended in a decision, and sometimes I move on to keep us on time. I don't really know what happens with those topics afterward. Things do come back up at later meetings, but I couldn't tell whether they're the ones I moved on from. Whoever's free takes notes, and these end up in an email, the shared folder or on paper. People then start on their part, and sometimes that work gets redone when the decision comes back up. Recent examples of reopened decisions are the registration form wording, whether lunch is offered at every site, and what time drop-off opens. The reasons they come back vary. Lunch came back after a coordinator had missed the meeting where it was discussed. Drop-off time came back after the director heard something new from a site's landlord following the decision. The registration form has been redone more than once, mostly because people remembered agreeing to different wording. Other times, too, someone says that's not what they thought was agreed. One coordinator has said, "I never know what's actually decided." For me, the meetings feel longer and more tiring than they used to, though I can't say how much time it has cost. Registration is meant to open early in the new year, and families keep asking when. Before it can open, the form has to be final, and I'd think families would need to know about lunch and the drop-off time before they sign up. I couldn't say whether the form wording is settled now, and I don't know where the lunch and drop-off time decisions stand.
